if (nzchar(params$condaenv)) reticulate::use_condaenv(params$condaenv, required = TRUE)

dir.create(OUT, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)
knitr::opts_chunk$set(fig.path = file.path(normalizePath(OUT), "figures", ""))
SEEDS <- as.integer(strsplit(params$seeds, ",")[[1]])
STATE_OFFSET <- 1e-4
LENGTHS <- c(30, 61, 90, 120, 180, 270, 365)
POSITIONS <- c("beginning", "middle", "end")
COLS <- c(SEIR = "#1b7837", SIR = "#2166ac")
METHOD_COLS <- c(BiLSTM = "forestgreen", `ABC-MCMC` = "firebrick", `ABC-SMC` = "purple", DE = "goldenrod", NelderMead = "steelblue")
METHODS <- names(METHOD_COLS)
BASELINES <- METHODS[-1]
SIM  <- file.path(R, params$sim_folder)
REAL <- file.path(R, params$real_folder)
tab <- function(x, digits = 3, ...) knitr::kable(x, format = "html", digits = digits, row.names = FALSE,
                                                table.attr = "class='table table-condensed' style='width:auto'", ...)
# Table and figure numbers, in the order they appear.
tn <- local({ i <- 0; function(txt) { i <<- i + 1; sprintf("Table %d. %s", i, txt) } })
fc <- local({ i <- 0; function(txt) { i <<- i + 1; sprintf("Figure %d. %s", i, txt) } })
fig <- function(...) {
  f <- file.path(R, ...); f <- f[file.exists(f)]
  if (length(f)) knitr::include_graphics(normalizePath(f), rel_path = FALSE)
}
FOLDERS <- local({ s <- strsplit(strsplit(params$model_folders, ";")[[1]], "="); setNames(vapply(s, `[`, "", 2), vapply(s, `[`, "", 1)) })
INFO <- list(
  SEIR = list(dir = file.path(R, FOLDERS[["SEIR"]]), known = c("n", "recov", "incub"), crate = c(5, 15),
              states = c("exposed_share", "infected_share", "recovered_share")),
  SIR  = list(dir = file.path(R, FOLDERS[["SIR"]]), known = c("n", "recov"), crate = c(1, 5),
              states = c("infected_share", "recovered_share"))
)
predict_model <- function(M, curves, known) {
  info <- INFO[[M]]
  known <- as.data.frame(known)[, info$known, drop = FALSE]
  curves <- unname(curves)
  ests <- lapply(file.path(info$dir, paste0("model_seed_", SEEDS)), function(d)
    bilstm_predict_many(d, curves, known, device = params$device))
  avg <- Reduce(`+`, ests) / length(ests)
  avg$crate <- avg$R0 * known$recov / avg$ptran
  avg
}
informative_days <- function(curve, k = 7) {
  r <- rle(as.numeric(curve) == 0); hit <- which(r$values & r$lengths >= k)[1]
  if (is.na(hit)) length(curve) else sum(r$lengths[seq_len(hit)]) - r$lengths[hit]
}
f2 <- function(x, d = 2) formatC(x, digits = d, format = "f")
pct <- function(x) sprintf("%.0f%%", x)
rng <- function(x, d = 2) paste(formatC(range(x), digits = d, format = "f"), collapse = "-")
hp_txt <- function(M) {
  cfg <- jsonlite::read_json(file.path(INFO[[M]]$dir, "model_seed_122", "model_config.json"))
  sprintf("%d layers of %d units, dropout %.2f, learning rate %.1e%s, batch %d, %d epochs", cfg$num_layers,
          cfg$hidden_size, cfg$dropout, cfg$learning_rate,
          if (identical(cfg$lr_schedule, "cosine")) " falling to 1% of it" else "", cfg$batch_size, cfg$epochs)
}
blank_repeats <- function(x, col) { x[[col]][duplicated(x[[col]])] <- ""; x }
```

```{r sim-compute}
# The BiLSTM alone on the noise-free test epidemics: windows of each length at the
# beginning, middle and end of each epidemic, as in Clean_any_length.Rmd; estimates cached.
sim <- lapply(setNames(names(INFO), names(INFO)), function(M) {
  info <- INFO[[M]]
  test <- readRDS(file.path(info$dir, "test_bank.rds"))
  active <- apply(test$cases, 1, informative_days)
  win_start <- function(pos, L, a) switch(pos, beginning = 1, middle = floor((a - L) / 2) + 1, end = a - L + 1)
  g <- expand.grid(length = LENGTHS, position = POSITIONS, curve = seq_len(nrow(test$theta)), stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
  g <- g[active[g$curve] >= g$length, ]
  g$start <- mapply(win_start, g$position, g$length, active[g$curve])
  cache <- file.path(OUT, paste0("simulated_estimates_", basename(info$dir), ".csv"))
  if (file.exists(cache)) {
    e <- read.csv(cache)
  } else {
    curves <- lapply(seq_len(nrow(g)), function(k) test$cases[g$curve[k], g$start[k]:(g$start[k] + g$length[k] - 1)])
    e <- predict_model(M, curves, test$theta[g$curve, ])[, c("R0", "ptran", "crate")]
    write.csv(e, cache, row.names = FALSE)
  }
  th <- test$theta[g$curve, ]
  lo <- info$crate[1]; hi <- info$crate[2]
  data.frame(model = M, g, R0_true = th$R0, ptran_true = th$ptran, crate_true = th$crate,
             R0 = e$R0, ptran = e$ptran, crate = e$crate,
             # Best guesses when R0 is known exactly but the split into ptran and crate is not.
             ptran_baseline = th$R0 * th$recov * log(hi / lo) / (hi - lo), crate_baseline = (lo + hi) / 2)
})
sim_all <- do.call(rbind, sim)
mae_by <- function(d) data.frame(
  windows = nrow(d),
  R0_MAE = mean(abs(d$R0 - d$R0_true)),
  ptran_MAE = mean(abs(d$ptran - d$ptran_true)), ptran_baseline_MAE = mean(abs(d$ptran_baseline - d$ptran_true)),
  crate_MAE = mean(abs(d$crate - d$crate_true)), crate_baseline_MAE = mean(abs(d$crate_baseline - d$crate_true)))
sim_tab <- do.call(rbind, lapply(names(INFO), function(M) do.call(rbind, lapply(LENGTHS, function(L) {
  d <- sim_all[sim_all$model == M & sim_all$length == L & sim_all$position == "beginning", ]
  if (!nrow(d)) return(NULL)
  cbind(model = M, length = L, mae_by(d),
        R0_MAE_all_positions = mean(abs(sim_all$R0 - sim_all$R0_true)[sim_all$model == M & sim_all$length == L]))
}))))
extras <- do.call(rbind, lapply(names(INFO), function(M) {
  rr <- read.csv(file.path(INFO[[M]]$dir, "R0_range_check.csv"), check.names = FALSE)
  cv <- read.csv(file.path(INFO[[M]]$dir, "coverage_by_length_and_position.csv"))
  data.frame(model = M, length = LENGTHS,
             R0_in_range = as.numeric(rr[match(LENGTHS, rr[[1]]), 2]),
             cov_new = vapply(LENGTHS, function(L) mean(cv$new_infections[cv$length == L]), 0),
             cov_infected = vapply(LENGTHS, function(L) mean(cv$currently_infected[cv$length == L]), 0))
}))
sim_tab <- merge(sim_tab, extras, by = c("model", "length"), sort = FALSE)
write.csv(sim_tab, file.path(OUT, "simulated_results.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
s_row <- function(M, L, col) sim_tab[[col]][sim_tab$model == M & sim_tab$length == L]
rng_txt <- function(M) paste(round(range(sim_tab$R0_in_range[sim_tab$model == M])), collapse = "-")
```

}))))

  }))))))

# Summary

**What was done.** Two BiLSTM models, one for SEIR and one for SIR, were trained on
**noise-free simulated epidemics** (every new infection counted) to estimate R0, ptran and
crate, and the state of the epidemic at the start of the window, from a window of daily new
infections of **any length from 30 to 365 days**, taken from the beginning, middle or end of an
epidemic. Known values: population `n`, recovery rate `recov` and (SEIR) incubation period
`incub`. Each model is the average of 5 networks trained on 1,000,000 simulated epidemics.
The BiLSTM was then compared with four standard calibration methods (ABC-MCMC, ABC-SMC,
differential evolution and Nelder-Mead) on simulated windows, where the truth is known, and on
real data: COVID-19 waves in 10 US states, Utah COVID-19 and influenza, and Baltimore 1918.

**Main findings**

1. **R0 is estimated accurately on simulated data, and better with longer windows.** For
   windows starting at the beginning of an epidemic, the R0 error falls from
   `r f2(s_row("SEIR", 30, "R0_MAE"))` (SEIR) and `r f2(s_row("SIR", 30, "R0_MAE"))` (SIR) at
   30 days to `r f2(s_row("SEIR", 180, "R0_MAE"))` and `r f2(s_row("SIR", 180, "R0_MAE"))` at
   180 days. The true R0 is inside the model's 95% range
   `r rng_txt("SEIR")`% (SEIR) and `r rng_txt("SIR")`% (SIR) of the time, depending on the window length.
2. **ptran and crate cannot be estimated separately.** Only their combination
   R0 = ptran x crate / recov shapes an epidemic curve. The crate error is no better than always
   guessing the middle of its range, and the ptran error is about the same as knowing R0
   exactly and guessing the split.
3. **The epidemic is recovered well.** Simulating the model forward from its estimates, the
   true daily new infections are inside the 95% band on 96-99% of days at every window
   length, and the number currently infected (which the model never sees) on 94-99% of days.
4. **Against standard calibration methods** (simulated windows, true values known; ABC-MCMC,
   ABC-SMC, DE and Nelder-Mead with their default settings), the BiLSTM's R0 error is
   `r f2(sim_get("SEIR", "BiLSTM", "R0 MAE"))` (SEIR) and `r f2(sim_get("SIR", "BiLSTM", "R0 MAE"))`
   (SIR), against `r rng(sapply(BASELINES, function(m) sim_get("SEIR", m, "R0 MAE")))` and
   `r rng(sapply(BASELINES, function(m) sim_get("SIR", m, "R0 MAE")))`. It also recovers the starting
   state and the hidden number currently infected best. Near the beginning of an epidemic the
   baselines come close; in the middle and at the end they are several times less accurate.
   DE matches the *observed* curve about as closely as the BiLSTM.
5. **On real data** there are no true parameter values; methods are compared by how well their
   simulated curves cover the observed counts. On COVID-19 waves of **10 US states** the BiLSTM
   covers `r pct(real_get("SEIR", "US states", "BiLSTM", "Coverage (%)"))` (SEIR) and
   `r pct(real_get("SIR", "US states", "BiLSTM", "Coverage (%)"))` (SIR) of the observed days,
   close to ABC-MCMC and ABC-SMC and above DE and Nelder-Mead. On **Utah COVID-19** cases the
   package's ABC-MCMC fits best (`r pct(utah_cov("SEIR", "ABC-MCMC"))` vs
   `r pct(utah_cov("SEIR", "BiLSTM"))` for the BiLSTM, SEIR): those case reports have weekday
   swings, reporting spikes and several waves, which noise-free training curves do not have.
6. **Improving the BiLSTM:** a new hyperparameter search alone did not help; training on
   1,000,000 instead of 300,000 epidemics with a falling learning rate made R0 errors 3-12%
   smaller for windows from the beginning of an epidemic, but did not change windows from the end.
7. **Speed:** a BiLSTM estimate takes about `r f2(speed[["BiLSTM"]], 3)` seconds per window
   (one network pass for many windows); the baselines take on average
   `r round(speed[["NelderMead"]])` seconds (Nelder-Mead), `r round(speed[["ABC-MCMC"]])` seconds
   (ABC-MCMC), `r round(speed[["DE"]] / 60, 1)` minutes (DE) and `r round(speed[["ABC-SMC"]] / 60, 1)`
   minutes (ABC-SMC) per window, after a one-time cost of simulating the training epidemics and
   training the networks (Section "Computational cost").

**Using the package.** Everything here can be done with the package's functions; the section
"Using the package: a guide" shows how (calibrating with the BiLSTM and the standard methods,
ptran and crate, predictions and scores, comparing methods with plots, the real data shipped
with the package, and training your own model).

# Setup

## The models

| | SEIR | SIR |
|---|---|---|
| Model (epiworldR) | `ModelSEIRCONN` | `ModelSIRCONN` |
| Known | `n` (5,000-10,000), `recov` (0.071-0.25), `incub` (1-21 days) | `n`, `recov` |
| Estimated | R0 (0.8-5), ptran, crate (5-15), and the state at the window start | R0 (0.8-5), ptran, crate (1-5), and the state at the window start |
| Training data | 1,000,000 simulated epidemics of 365 days, noise-free | same |
| Network | BiLSTM, `r hp_txt("SEIR")`; average of 5 seeds | BiLSTM, `r hp_txt("SIR")`; average of 5 seeds |
| Window lengths | 30 to 365 days, from the beginning, middle or end of an epidemic | same |

## The methods compared

The BiLSTM and four standard calibration methods, used as someone with basic knowledge of them
would use them. All get the same windows, known values (`n`, `recov`, and `incub` for SEIR) and
ranges: R0 between 0.8 and 5 and the state on the first day of the window (the baselines search
the shares exposed, infectious and recovered on the log10 scale, 0.0001 to 0.4, 0.95 for
recovered), with the contact rate fixed at the middle of its range (only R0 shapes a curve).
The baselines fit the observed daily counts by least squares (root mean squared error for the
package's ABC methods); DE and Nelder-Mead use one model run with a fixed seed per candidate,
so the same candidate always gets the same fit. Code: `methods_common.R`.

| Method | Library and settings | Model runs per window | What the user must decide |
|---|---|---|---|
| BiLSTM | this package: one pass of the trained network (average of 5 seeds), with an R0 range from similar calibration windows | none | nothing: the daily counts and the known values |
| ABC-MCMC | this package (`make_calibrator("ABC-MCMC")`), defaults: 3,000 random-walk steps (1,500 burn-in), proposal sd 8% of each range, tolerance 0.30 x the size of the counts | 3,000 | ranges, chain length, tolerance, step size |
| ABC-SMC | this package (`make_calibrator("ABC-SMC")`), defaults (200 particles, 6 generations, each tolerance the median distance of the previous generation) with its limits raised to 30,000 model runs and 20,000 attempts per generation so that it finishes | up to 30,000 | ranges, particles, generations, tolerances, budget |
| DE | `DEoptim`, defaults: population 10 x the number of unknowns, 200 generations, F = 0.8, CR = 0.5 | 6,000-8,000 | ranges, population, generations |
| Nelder-Mead | `stats::optim`, defaults, started at the middle of the ranges; values outside the ranges rejected | 100-500 | ranges, starting point |

## How the methods are scored

**Parameter errors** (simulated data only, where the true values are known). For $N$ windows
with true value $\theta_i$ and estimate $\hat\theta_i$,

$$\text{MAE} = \frac{1}{N}\sum_{i=1}^{N} \left|\hat\theta_i - \theta_i\right| .$$

The **starting state error** is the same for the shares of the population in each state on the
first day of the window (exposed, infectious, recovered), averaged over the states, in
percentage points.

**Bands.** Each method's estimates are run 500 times in `ModelSEIRCONN` / `ModelSIRCONN` from
its estimated starting state (with parameters drawn from its uncertainty: the BiLSTM's R0
range, the ABC posteriors; DE and Nelder-Mead give one estimate, so their bands show only the
randomness of the epidemic). Each day's simulated count is the number of people who became
infectious that day (E to I for SEIR, S to I for SIR). On each day $t$ this gives a 95% band
from $l_t$ (2.5% of the runs below) to $u_t$ (2.5% above) and a median $m_t$. The band is
compared with the value $y_t$: the true daily new infections and the true number currently
infectious on simulated data, the observed daily counts on real data, over the $T$ days of the
window, and over the 14 days after the window (*prediction*).

**Coverage** is the share of days inside the band (higher is better; about 95% is ideal):

$$\text{coverage} = \frac{100}{T}\sum_{t=1}^{T} \mathbf{1}\left(l_t \le y_t \le u_t\right) \ \%.$$

**Interval score** (Gneiting and Raftery, 2007). Coverage alone can be won by a very wide band.
The interval score rewards narrow bands and punishes days outside the band by how far outside
they are:

$$\text{IS} = \frac{1}{T}\sum_{t=1}^{T}\left[(u_t - l_t) + \frac{2}{\alpha}\,(l_t - y_t)\,\mathbf{1}(y_t < l_t) + \frac{2}{\alpha}\,(y_t - u_t)\,\mathbf{1}(y_t > u_t)\right], \qquad \alpha = 0.05,\ \tfrac{2}{\alpha} = 40.$$

In words: on each day, the **width of the band**, plus, if the value is outside the band,
**40 times the distance to the band**; then the average over the days. It is in the units of
the counts (daily cases), and **lower is better**. Example with a band from 10 to 30:

| Value on the day | Inside? | Interval score for the day |
|---|---|---|
| 25 | yes | 30 - 10 = 20 |
| 35 | no, 5 above | 20 + 40 x 5 = 220 |
| 8 | no, 2 below | 20 + 40 x 2 = 100 |

A band from 0 to 100 that always holds the value scores 100 every day, so a band five times
narrower that holds the value scores better, but each missed day costs 40 times the miss. The
factor 40 comes from the 95% level: missing by a little is cheap, missing by a lot is not, and
a method that states a 95% band but misses often is punished. The interval score depends on
the size of the counts, so it is compared between methods on the same data, not between datasets.

**Error of the median** is the average distance between the median curve and the values,
$\frac{1}{T}\sum_t |m_t - y_t|$, in daily counts.

# Simulated data (no noise): the BiLSTM

## Errors by window length

Windows starting at the beginning of an epidemic. *Baseline*: the best possible guess for
ptran and crate when R0 is known exactly (ptran from R0 and the average of 1/crate; crate =
the middle of its range). *R0 MAE, any position*: the same, averaged over windows from the
beginning, middle and end. *Coverage*: share of days on which the true count is inside the
95% band of 100 simulations from the model's estimates.

```{r sim-tables, results="asis"}
nice <- function(M) {
  d <- sim_tab[sim_tab$model == M, ]
  d <- d[order(d$length), ]
  data.frame(`Window (days)` = d$length, `Test windows` = d$windows, `R0 MAE` = d$R0_MAE,
             `ptran MAE` = d$ptran_MAE, `ptran MAE, baseline` = d$ptran_baseline_MAE,
             `crate MAE` = d$crate_MAE, `crate MAE, baseline` = d$crate_baseline_MAE,
             `R0 MAE, any position` = d$R0_MAE_all_positions, `True R0 in 95% range (%)` = d$R0_in_range,
             `Coverage: new infections (%)` = d$cov_new, `Coverage: currently infected (%)` = d$cov_infected,
             check.names = FALSE)
}
cat(tab(nice("SEIR"), digits = 3, caption = tn("SEIR on noise-free simulated data")), sep = "\n")
cat(tab(nice("SIR"), digits = 3, caption = tn("SIR on noise-free simulated data")), sep = "\n")
```

A window is used only if the test epidemic is still going for that many days, so there are
fewer long windows, especially for SIR (about 70% of the SIR test epidemics end within 90
days). The results for 270 and 365 days rest on few epidemics.

```{r sim-fig, fig.width=12, fig.height=4, fig.cap=fc("Mean absolute error by window length (windows starting at the beginning of an epidemic). Dashed: the baseline for ptran and crate.")}
op <- par(mfrow = c(1, 3), mar = c(4.5, 4.5, 3, 1))
for (p in c("R0", "ptran", "crate")) {
  col <- paste0(p, "_MAE"); base <- paste0(p, "_baseline_MAE")
  yl <- range(c(0, sim_tab[[col]], if (p != "R0") sim_tab[[base]]))
  plot(NA, xlim = range(LENGTHS), ylim = yl, xlab = "window length (days)", ylab = paste(p, "MAE"), main = p)
  for (M in names(INFO)) {
    d <- sim_tab[sim_tab$model == M, ]; d <- d[order(d$length), ]
    lines(d$length, d[[col]], type = "b", pch = 16, lwd = 2, col = COLS[[M]])
    if (p != "R0") lines(d$length, d[[base]], lty = 2, lwd = 1.5, col = COLS[[M]])
  }
  if (p == "R0") legend("topright", bty = "n", lwd = 2, pch = 16, col = COLS, legend = names(COLS))
}
par(op)
```

```{r sim-scatter, fig.width=12, fig.height=7.5, fig.cap=fc("Estimated vs true R0 for windows of 30, 90 and 180 days from the beginning of an epidemic. The line is perfect agreement.")}
op <- par(mfrow = c(2, 3), mar = c(4.5, 4.5, 3, 1))
for (M in names(INFO)) for (L in c(30, 90, 180)) {
  d <- sim_all[sim_all$model == M & sim_all$length == L & sim_all$position == "beginning", ]
  plot(d$R0_true, d$R0, pch = 16, cex = 0.5, col = adjustcolor(COLS[[M]], 0.5), xlim = c(0.7, 5.1), ylim = c(0.7, 5.1),
       xlab = "true R0", ylab = "estimated R0", main = sprintf("%s, %d days (MAE %.2f, %d windows)", M, L,
                                                             mean(abs(d$R0 - d$R0_true)), nrow(d)))
  abline(0, 1, lty = 2)
}
par(op)
```

Coverage on each day of the window (share of windows whose true daily new infections are
inside the 95% band on that day), for each window length:

```{r sim-coverage-figs, out.width="100%", fig.cap=c(fc("Coverage of daily new infections through time, SEIR. Dashed line: 95%."), fc("The same for SIR."))}
fig(FOLDERS[["SEIR"]], "figures", "coverage-by-day-plot-1.png")
fig(FOLDERS[["SIR"]], "figures", "coverage-by-day-plot-1.png")
```

## Making the BiLSTM better: three versions

Three versions of each model were trained and tested on the same 1,000 test epidemics:

| Version | What it is |
|---|---|
| Current | settings tuned earlier for an older SEIR model; 300,000 training epidemics; 100 epochs at a constant learning rate |
| Tuned | settings from a new search for this model (40 trials of 20 epochs; score: validation error of R0 and the starting state); otherwise as Current |
| Big (used in this report) | the tuned settings, 1,000,000 training epidemics, and a learning rate that falls smoothly over 50 epochs |

```{r versions, results="asis"}
VERSIONS <- c(Current = "clean", Tuned = "clean_tuned", Big = "clean_big")
ver <- do.call(rbind, lapply(names(INFO), function(M) do.call(rbind, lapply(names(VERSIONS), function(v) {
  d <- file.path(R, paste0(tolower(M), "_", VERSIONS[[v]]))
  r0 <- read.csv(file.path(d, "R0_MAE_by_length_and_position.csv"))
  b <- function(L) r0$R0_abs_error[r0$length == L & r0$position == "beginning"]
  rr <- read.csv(file.path(d, "R0_range_check.csv"), check.names = FALSE)
  cv <- read.csv(file.path(d, "coverage_by_length_and_position.csv"))
  ao <- read.csv(file.path(d, "all_outputs.csv"))
  data.frame(Model = M, Version = v, `30 days` = b(30), `61 days` = b(61), `90 days` = b(90), `180 days` = b(180),
             `All windows` = mean(r0$R0_abs_error), `True R0 in 95% range (%)` = rr[rr[[1]] == "all", 2],
             `Coverage: new infections (%)` = mean(cv$new_infections),
             `Starting state error` = mean(ao$MAE[grepl("^log share", ao$output)]), check.names = FALSE)
}))))
cat(tab(blank_repeats(ver, "Model"), digits = 3, caption = tn(paste("R0 MAE of the three versions: windows from the beginning of an",
  "epidemic (30-180 days) and all 21 window lengths and positions; the 95% R0 range; coverage of daily new",
  "infections; and the starting-state error (mean absolute error of the log shares at the window start)"))), sep = "\n")
```

The **tuned** settings alone did not help: their advantage after 20 epochs on 100,000
epidemics did not carry over to full training. The **big** version is a little better than
the current one: R0 errors fall by about 3-12% for windows from the beginning of an epidemic
up to 120 days, and the starting state is estimated about 5% better. Windows from the **end**
of an epidemic did not improve with any change. On the earlier real datasets the big version
was not better overall:

```{r versions-real, results="asis"}
rv <- lapply(c(Current = "clean_real_data", Big = "clean_real_data_big"), function(f) {
  x <- read.csv(file.path(R, f, "results_by_window.csv")); x[x$method == "BiLSTM", ]
})
rt <- do.call(rbind, lapply(names(INFO), function(M) {
  ds <- unique(rv$Current$dataset)
  cv <- sapply(rv, function(x) vapply(ds, function(dn) mean(x$coverage[x$model == M & x$dataset == dn]), 0))
  rbind(data.frame(Model = M, Dataset = ds, cv, check.names = FALSE),
        data.frame(Model = M, Dataset = "All datasets", t(colMeans(sapply(rv, function(x) x$coverage[x$model == M]))),
                   check.names = FALSE))
}))
names(rt)[3:4] <- c("Current version: coverage (%)", "Big version: coverage (%)")
cat(tab(blank_repeats(rt, "Model"), digits = 0, caption = tn("BiLSTM coverage of the observed daily counts on the earlier real datasets (windows of 30-180 days ending a week after the peak): current vs big version")), sep = "\n")
```

# Simulated data: the BiLSTM against standard methods

The test where the truth is known: 9 windows for each model, window length (30, 61, 120 and
180 days) and position (beginning, middle, end), 108 windows per model, from the test
epidemics of the noise-free models.

## Summary

```{r sim-summary, results="asis"}
show <- function(cols, digits, caption) {
  x <- sim_summary[, c("Model", "Method", cols)]
  cat(tab(blank_repeats(x, "Model"), digits = digits, caption = tn(caption)), sep = "\n")
}
show(c("Windows (failed)", "R0 MAE", "R0 MAE: beginning", "R0 MAE: middle", "R0 MAE: end", "True R0 in 95% range (%)",
       "Starting state error (% points)", "Seconds per window", "Model runs per window"), 2,
     "Parameter recovery and cost. BiLSTM seconds: one network pass for all windows of a model, divided by the number of windows.")
show(c("Coverage: new infections (%)", "Coverage: currently infected (%)", "Coverage: next 14 days (%)",
       "Interval score: new infections", "Interval score: currently infected", "Interval score: next 14 days"), 1,
     "Trajectories and prediction: coverage (higher is better) and interval score (lower is better) of the true daily new infections in the window, of the true number currently infectious (which no method sees), and of the daily new infections in the 14 days after the window.")
```

}

  plot(NA, xlim = range(a$length), ylim = c(0, max(a$error)), xlab = "window length (days)", ylab = "R0 MAE", main = paste(M, "-", pos))

  }

## Trajectories and prediction by position

```{r sim-traj, results="asis"}
for (M in names(INFO)) {
  d <- sbr_ok[sbr_ok$model == M, ]
  out <- do.call(rbind, lapply(POSITIONS, function(p) do.call(rbind, lapply(METHODS, function(m) {
    x <- d[d$position == p & d$method == m, ]
    data.frame(Position = p, Method = m, `Coverage: new infections` = mean(x$cov_new),
               `Coverage: currently infected` = mean(x$cov_infected), `Coverage: next 14 days` = mean(x$cov_future, na.rm = TRUE),
               `Interval score: new infections` = mean(x$IS_new), `Interval score: currently infected` = mean(x$IS_infected),
               `Interval score: next 14 days` = mean(x$IS_future, na.rm = TRUE), check.names = FALSE)
  }))))
  cat(tab(blank_repeats(out, "Position"), digits = 1, caption = tn(sprintf("%s: coverage (%%) and interval score by window position, simulated windows", M))), sep = "\n")
}
```

## How sure can we be? (paired comparison)

For every window, each baseline's R0 error minus the BiLSTM's on the **same** window (positive:
the BiLSTM is more accurate), with a 95% bootstrap interval over windows.

```{r sim-paired, results="asis"}
set.seed(3)
pair <- merge(sbr_ok[sbr_ok$method != "BiLSTM", c("id", "model", "position", "method", "error")],
              sbr_ok[sbr_ok$method == "BiLSTM", c("id", "error")], by = "id", suffixes = c("", "_bilstm"))
pt <- do.call(rbind, lapply(names(INFO), function(M) do.call(rbind, lapply(BASELINES, function(m) {
  do.call(rbind, lapply(c("all", POSITIONS), function(pos) {
    p <- pair[pair$model == M & pair$method == m & (pos == "all" | pair$position == pos), ]
    if (nrow(p) < 2) return(NULL)
    dlt <- p$error - p$error_bilstm
    ci <- quantile(replicate(2000, mean(sample(dlt, replace = TRUE))), c(0.025, 0.975), names = FALSE)
    data.frame(Model = M, Method = m, Windows = pos, n = nrow(p), `Mean difference` = mean(dlt),
               `95% interval` = sprintf("%.3f to %.3f", ci[1], ci[2]),
               `BiLSTM more accurate (% of windows)` = 100 * mean(p$error_bilstm < p$error), check.names = FALSE)
  }))
}))))
cat(tab(blank_repeats(pt, "Model"), digits = 3, caption = tn("Paired difference in R0 error, simulated windows")), sep = "\n")
```

# Real data: the BiLSTM against standard methods

## The data and the windows

- **US states:** daily COVID-19 cases (Johns Hopkins University) in the 10 states that reported
  cases every day, with no negative corrections, in all three waves (fall 2020, Delta 2021,
  Omicron 2021-22), scaled to cases per 10,000 people, `n = 10,000`. (States that skipped
  weekends have zeros on about 30% of the days, which a noise-free model reads as no new
  infections.)
- **Utah and Baltimore:** Utah COVID-19 cases (the last year of the Utah data, 2024-25, and the
  summer 2023 wave), Utah influenza hospital admissions (2022-23 and 2023-24 seasons) and
  Baltimore influenza cases in 1918.
- **Windows:** 30, 60 and 90 days at the **beginning**, the **middle** (centred on the peak)
  and the **end** of each wave (windows longer than a wave are skipped). Known values:
  COVID-19 `recov` = 1/7, `incub` = 5 days; influenza `recov` = 0.25, `incub` = 2 days.

```{r real-data-table, results="asis"}
w1 <- real[real$model == "SEIR" & real$method == "BiLSTM", ]
dt <- aggregate(id ~ group + wave, w1, length)
dt <- dt[order(dt$group != "Utah and Baltimore", match(dt$wave, names(rwaves))), ]
names(dt) <- c("Data group", "Wave", "Windows")
cat(tab(blank_repeats(dt, "Data group"), digits = 0, caption = tn("The waves and the number of windows in each (per model)")), sep = "\n")
```

```{r real-data-plot, fig.width=13, fig.height=19, fig.cap=fc("Daily counts in each wave (blue; US states: cases per 10,000 people). Grey bars: the 60-day windows at the beginning, middle and end.")}
op <- par(mfrow = c(ceiling(length(rwaves) / 3), 3), mar = c(2, 4, 2, 0.5))
for (v in rwaves) {
  plot(v$x, v$y, type = "l", col = "blue", xlab = "", ylab = "daily count", main = v$name, cex.main = 0.9)
  usr <- par("usr")
  for (j in seq_along(POSITIONS)) {
    w <- Filter(function(z) z$wave == v$name && z$length == 60 && z$position == POSITIONS[j], rwin)
    if (!length(w)) next
    w <- w[[1]]; yy <- usr[4] - j * (usr[4] - usr[3]) * 0.05
    segments(w$x[1], yy, w$x[w$length], yy, lwd = 3, col = "grey40")
  }
}
par(op)
```

## How to read the tables

- **Overall**: one row per model, data group and method, averaged over **all** windows of the
  group (every wave, window length and position): `r sum(w1$group == "US states")` windows for the
  US states and `r sum(w1$group != "US states")` for Utah and Baltimore.
- **By window length and position**: the same, split by window length and by where the window
  sits in the wave (beginning, middle around the peak, end).
- **By wave**: one row per wave (for example "New York fall 2020"), averaged over its windows
  (3 lengths x 3 positions = 9 windows, fewer for short waves). "Utah COVID-19 2024-25" is the
  last year of the Utah data rather than a single wave.
- Real data have no true values: all measures compare the bands with the **observed** daily
  counts (Section 2.3). The interval score is in daily counts, so it is compared between
  methods on the same data, not between datasets.

## Overall

```{r real-overall, results="asis"}
x <- real_summary[, c("Model", "Data", "Method", "Windows (failed)", "Coverage (%)", "Interval score", "Band width",
                      "Error of the median", "Coverage: next 14 days (%)", "Interval score: next 14 days", "Seconds per window")]
cat(tab(blank_repeats(x, "Model"), digits = 1, caption = tn("Real data: coverage and interval score of the observed daily counts in the window and in the 14 days after it, mean band width, error of the median, and time")), sep = "\n")
```

## By window length and position

```{r real-cells, results="asis"}
cell_table <- function(M, g, what) {
  a <- aggregate(as.formula(paste(what, "~ position + length + method")), real_ok[real_ok$model == M & real_ok$group == g, ], mean)
  w <- reshape(a, idvar = c("position", "length"), timevar = "method", direction = "wide")
  names(w) <- sub(paste0("^", what, "\\."), "", names(w))
  w <- w[order(match(w$position, POSITIONS), w$length), c("position", "length", intersect(METHODS, names(w)))]
  names(w)[1:2] <- c("Position", "Window (days)")
  blank_repeats(w, "Position")
}
for (g in c("US states", "Utah and Baltimore")) for (M in names(INFO)) {
  cat(tab(cell_table(M, g, "coverage"), digits = 0, caption = tn(sprintf("%s, %s: coverage (%%) of the observed daily counts", M, g))), sep = "\n")
  cat(tab(cell_table(M, g, "interval_score"), digits = 1, caption = tn(sprintf("%s, %s: interval score", M, g))), sep = "\n")
}
```

```{r real-cell-fig, fig.width=13, fig.height=8, fig.cap=fc("US states: coverage by window length, for windows at the beginning, middle and end of the waves. Dashed: 95%.")}
op <- par(mfrow = c(2, 3), mar = c(4.5, 4.5, 3, 1))
for (M in names(INFO)) for (pos in POSITIONS) {
  a <- aggregate(coverage ~ length + method, real_ok[real_ok$model == M & real_ok$group == "US states" & real_ok$position == pos, ], mean)
  plot(NA, xlim = range(a$length), ylim = c(0, 100), xlab = "window length (days)", ylab = "coverage %", main = paste(M, "-", pos))
  abline(h = 95, lty = 2)
  for (m in METHODS) {
    x <- a[a$method == m, ]; x <- x[order(x$length), ]
    lines(x$length, x$coverage, type = "b", pch = 16, lwd = if (m == "BiLSTM") 3 else 1.5, col = METHOD_COLS[[m]])
  }
  if (M == "SEIR" && pos == "beginning") legend("bottomleft", bty = "n", lwd = 2, pch = 16, col = METHOD_COLS, legend = METHODS)
}
par(op)
```

## R0 estimates

The 60-day windows around the peak of the Utah and Baltimore data. The BiLSTM's ptran and crate
are shown for completeness: as on simulated data, only R0 carries information.

```{r real-r0, results="asis"}
bil <- readRDS(file.path(REAL, "bilstm_fits.rds"))
for (M in names(INFO)) {
  d <- real[real$model == M & real$group == "Utah and Baltimore" & real$length == 60 & real$position == "middle", ]
  out <- do.call(rbind, lapply(unique(d$wave), function(u) {
    x <- d[d$wave == u, ]; b <- x[x$method == "BiLSTM", ]; f <- bil[[paste(M, b$id)]]
    ptran <- f$draws[[1]]$ptran; recov <- f$draws[[1]]$recov
    cell <- function(m) { y <- x[x$method == m, ]
      if (!nrow(y) || isTRUE(y$failed)) "failed" else if (is.na(y$R0_low)) sprintf("%.2f", y$R0) else
        sprintf("%.2f (%.2f-%.2f)", y$R0, y$R0_low, y$R0_high) }
    data.frame(Data = u, `BiLSTM R0 (95% range)` = cell("BiLSTM"), `BiLSTM ptran` = sprintf("%.3f", ptran),
               `BiLSTM crate` = sprintf("%.1f", b$R0 * recov / ptran),
               t(vapply(BASELINES, function(m) cell(m), "")), check.names = FALSE)
  }))
  cat(tab(out, caption = tn(sprintf("%s: R0 estimates (95%% range where the method gives one)", M))), sep = "\n")
}
```

## Examples

The 60-day windows (rows: waves; columns: beginning, middle, end). Blue: the observed counts;
green: the BiLSTM's 95% band and median; red dashed: ABC-MCMC's band; gold dotted: DE's band.
Panel titles: coverage of BiLSTM | ABC-MCMC | DE.

```{r real-examples-def}
example_groups <- list(`Utah COVID-19` = c("Utah COVID-19 2024-25", "Utah COVID-19 summer 2023"),
                       Influenza = c("Utah flu 2022-23", "Utah flu 2023-24", "Baltimore flu 1918"),
                       `New York` = grep("^New York ", names(rwaves), value = TRUE),
                       Texas = grep("^Texas ", names(rwaves), value = TRUE),
                       `North Dakota` = grep("^North Dakota ", names(rwaves), value = TRUE))
plot_examples <- function(M, waves_shown) {
  op <- par(mfrow = c(length(waves_shown), 3), mar = c(2.5, 4, 3, 0.5))
  for (wv in waves_shown) for (pos in POSITIONS) {
    w <- Filter(function(z) z$wave == wv && z$length == 60 && z$position == pos, rwin)
    if (!length(w)) { plot.new(); next }
    w <- w[[1]]; i <- seq_len(w$length)
    f <- lapply(setNames(c("BiLSTM", "ABC-MCMC", "DE"), c("BiLSTM", "ABC-MCMC", "DE")), function(m) rfit(M, w$id, m))
    top <- max(c(w$y, f$BiLSTM$band$upper[i], pmin(f$`ABC-MCMC`$band$upper[i], 2.5 * max(w$y))))
    plot(w$x, w$y, type = "n", ylim = c(0, top), xlab = "", ylab = "daily count", cex.main = 0.85,
         main = sprintf("%s, %s\n%.0f%% | %.0f%% | %.0f%%", wv, pos, f$BiLSTM$window[["coverage"]],
                        f$`ABC-MCMC`$window[["coverage"]], f$DE$window[["coverage"]]))
    b <- f$BiLSTM$band[i, ]
    polygon(c(w$x, rev(w$x)), c(b$upper, rev(b$lower)), col = adjustcolor("forestgreen", 0.3), border = NA)
    lines(w$x, b$median, col = "forestgreen", lwd = 2)
    lines(w$x, f$`ABC-MCMC`$band$upper[i], col = "firebrick", lty = 2); lines(w$x, f$`ABC-MCMC`$band$lower[i], col = "firebrick", lty = 2)
    lines(w$x, f$DE$band$upper[i], col = "goldenrod", lty = 3, lwd = 1.5); lines(w$x, f$DE$band$lower[i], col = "goldenrod", lty = 3, lwd = 1.5)
    lines(w$x, w$y, col = "blue", lwd = 1.3)
  }
  par(op)
}
```

# Predicting cases with the renewal equation

The bands above come from running the agent-based model 500 times from each method's
estimates. A faster way to turn the BiLSTM's estimates into a predicted curve is the
**renewal equation**: the number of people who become infectious on day $t$ is R0 times the
share still susceptible times the people infected before, weighted by how long ago,

$$C_t = R_0 \, \frac{S_{t-1}}{n} \sum_{k \ge 1} g_k \, C_{t-k},$$

where $g_k$ is the model's **generation interval**, the chance that an infection happens $k$
days after the infector was infected (SIR: the infectious time, mean $1/\text{recov}$ days; SEIR:
the incubation time, mean `incub` days, plus the infectious time). It gives the **average** curve
of the model, with no randomness. Only R0 is needed (ptran and crate enter only through
R0 = ptran x crate / recov). Because both waiting times in the model are geometric, the sum can
be carried day by day with the numbers exposed, infectious and susceptible (`renewal_curve()` in
`methods_common.R`); the people already exposed or infectious on the first day of the window
start it. Bands: one curve for each of the BiLSTM's parameter draws (its R0 range), and on each
day a Poisson count around the curve.

The renewal equation needs the state on the first day of the window (the **initial cases**).
Two ways are compared:

- **Renewal A**: the BiLSTM's own estimate of the starting state;
- **Renewal B**: the initial cases worked out **by the renewal equation**: with R0 fixed at the
  BiLSTM's estimate, the shares exposed, infectious and recovered on the first day that make
  the renewal curve closest to the observed counts (least squares; repeated for 30 values from
  the BiLSTM's R0 range to get a band).

```{r renewal-check, results="asis"}
source("methods_common.R")
chk <- do.call(rbind, lapply(c("SEIR", "SIR"), function(M) {
  info <- model_info(M)
  base <- list(n = 8000, recov = 0.15, incub = 4, ptran = if (M == "SEIR") 0.03 else 0.1, crate = if (M == "SEIR") 10 else 3)
  do.call(rbind, lapply(list(c(0.002, 0.001, 0), c(0.02, 0.05, 0.3)), function(s) {
    p <- c(base, list(exposed_share = if (M == "SEIR") s[1] else 0, infected_share = s[2], recovered_share = s[3]))
    abm <- rowMeans(vapply(1:200, function(k) run_model(info, p, 90, k)$new, numeric(90)))
    rn <- renewal_curve(info, p, 90)$new
    data.frame(Model = M, `Start: infectious, recovered (%)` = sprintf("%.1f, %.0f", 100 * s[2], 100 * s[3]),
               `Total, model (mean of 200 runs)` = sum(abm), `Total, renewal` = sum(rn),
               `Peak day, model` = which.max(abm), `Peak day, renewal` = which.max(rn),
               `Mean daily difference` = mean(abs(abm - rn)), `Peak size, model` = max(abm), check.names = FALSE)
  }))
}))
cat(tab(blank_repeats(chk, "Model"), digits = 1, caption = tn("The renewal equation against the agent-based model (R0 = 2, n = 8,000, 90 days)")), sep = "\n")
```

```{r renewal-compute}
CORES <- as.integer(Sys.getenv("SLURM_CPUS_PER_TASK", "1"))
n_b <- 30   # R0 values from the BiLSTM's range for renewal B
renewal_scores <- function(info, w_y, known, draws, R0_hat, days, truth_infected = NULL, future = numeric(0), true_state = NULL) {
  L <- length(w_y); i_win <- seq_len(L); i_fut <- L + seq_along(future)
  t0 <- proc.time()[["elapsed"]]
  bA <- renewal_band(info, draws, days)
  tA <- proc.time()[["elapsed"]] - t0
  t0 <- proc.time()[["elapsed"]]
  R0s <- stats::quantile(vapply(draws, function(p) p$ptran * p$crate / p$recov, 0), seq(0.02, 0.98, length.out = n_b), names = FALSE)
  drawsB <- lapply(R0s, function(r) renewal_initial_state(info, w_y, r, known))
  bB <- renewal_band(info, drawsB, days)
  tB <- proc.time()[["elapsed"]] - t0
  pB <- renewal_initial_state(info, w_y, R0_hat, known)
  one <- function(b, label, secs, state) {
    s_new <- score_band(b$new, w_y, i_win)
    s_fut <- if (length(future)) score_band(b$new, future, i_fut) else c(coverage = NA, interval_score = NA)
    s_inf <- if (!is.null(truth_infected)) score_band(b$infected, truth_infected, i_win) else c(coverage = NA, interval_score = NA)
    data.frame(approach = label, cov_new = s_new[["coverage"]], IS_new = s_new[["interval_score"]],
               cov_infected = s_inf[["coverage"]], IS_infected = s_inf[["interval_score"]],
               cov_future = s_fut[["coverage"]], IS_future = s_fut[["interval_score"]], seconds = secs,
               state_error = if (is.null(true_state)) NA else 100 * mean(abs(unlist(state[names(true_state)]) - true_state)))
  }
  rbind(one(bA, "Renewal A (BiLSTM state)", tA, draws[[1]]), one(bB, "Renewal B (initial cases by renewal)", tB, pB))
}
sim_file <- file.path(OUT, "renewal_simulated.csv")
if (!file.exists(sim_file)) {
  sw <- readRDS(file.path(SIM, "windows.rds")); sbil <- readRDS(file.path(SIM, "bilstm_fits.rds"))
  out <- parallel::mclapply(names(sw$windows), function(id) {
    set.seed(match(id, names(sw$windows)))
    w <- sw$windows[[id]]; tr <- sw$truth[[id]]; f <- sbil[[id]]; info <- model_info(w$model)
    st <- f$state[info$states]   # the BiLSTM's own state estimate (renewal A)
    draws <- f$draws
    d <- renewal_scores(info, w$y, w$known, draws, f$R0, w$length + length(tr$future), tr$infected, tr$future, w$state)
    d$state_error[1] <- 100 * mean(abs(st - w$state))
    cbind(model = w$model, id = id, position = w$position, length = w$length, d)
  }, mc.cores = CORES)
  write.csv(do.call(rbind, out), sim_file, row.names = FALSE)
}
ren_sim <- read.csv(sim_file)
real_file <- file.path(OUT, "renewal_real.csv")
if (!file.exists(real_file)) {
  rbil <- readRDS(file.path(REAL, "bilstm_fits.rds"))
  jobs <- expand.grid(M = names(INFO), id = names(rwin), stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
  out <- parallel::mclapply(seq_len(nrow(jobs)), function(k) {
    set.seed(k)
    M <- jobs$M[k]; w <- rwin[[jobs$id[k]]]; f <- rbil[[paste(M, w$id)]]; info <- model_info(M)
    d <- renewal_scores(info, w$y, w$known[info$known], f$draws, f$R0, w$length + length(w$future), NULL, w$future)
    cbind(model = M, id = w$id, group = w$group, wave = w$wave, position = w$position, length = w$length, d)
  }, mc.cores = CORES)
  write.csv(do.call(rbind, out), real_file, row.names = FALSE)
}
ren_real <- read.csv(real_file)
# Time of the 500 agent-based runs for a band, measured on a few windows for comparison.
abm_time <- local({
  sw <- readRDS(file.path(SIM, "windows.rds")); sbil <- readRDS(file.path(SIM, "bilstm_fits.rds"))
  ids <- names(sw$windows)[seq(1, length(sw$windows), length.out = 6)]
  vapply(ids, function(id) { w <- sw$windows[[id]]
    system.time(band_of(model_info(w$model), sbil[[id]]$draws, w$length + 14))[["elapsed"]] }, 0)
})
```

## Simulated windows

The BiLSTM's estimates turned into curves in three ways: running the agent-based model 500
times (as in the rest of the report), renewal A and renewal B.

```{r renewal-sim, results="asis"}
abm <- sbr_ok[sbr_ok$method == "BiLSTM", ]
row_of <- function(d, label, M) data.frame(Model = M, Approach = label,
  `Starting state error (% points)` = mean(d$state_error), `Coverage: new infections` = mean(d$cov_new),
  `Interval score: new infections` = mean(d$IS_new), `Coverage: currently infected` = mean(d$cov_infected),
  `Interval score: currently infected` = mean(d$IS_infected), `Coverage: next 14 days` = mean(d$cov_future, na.rm = TRUE),
  `Interval score: next 14 days` = mean(d$IS_future, na.rm = TRUE), check.names = FALSE)
rs_tab <- do.call(rbind, lapply(names(INFO), function(M) rbind(
  row_of(abm[abm$model == M, ], "Agent-based model, 500 runs", M),
  do.call(rbind, lapply(unique(ren_sim$approach), function(a) row_of(ren_sim[ren_sim$model == M & ren_sim$approach == a, ], a, M))))))
cat(tab(blank_repeats(rs_tab, "Model"), digits = 1, caption = tn("Simulated windows: the BiLSTM's estimates turned into curves by the agent-based model or by the renewal equation (starting state error: the starting state used)")), sep = "\n")
pos_tab <- do.call(rbind, lapply(names(INFO), function(M) do.call(rbind, lapply(POSITIONS, function(p) {
  a <- abm[abm$model == M & abm$position == p, ]; r <- ren_sim[ren_sim$model == M & ren_sim$position == p, ]
  data.frame(Model = M, Position = p,
             `Coverage, model 500 runs` = mean(a$cov_new),
             `Coverage, renewal A` = mean(r$cov_new[r$approach == unique(ren_sim$approach)[1]]),
             `Coverage, renewal B` = mean(r$cov_new[r$approach == unique(ren_sim$approach)[2]]),
             `State error, BiLSTM (A)` = mean(r$state_error[r$approach == unique(ren_sim$approach)[1]]),
             `State error, renewal (B)` = mean(r$state_error[r$approach == unique(ren_sim$approach)[2]]), check.names = FALSE)
}))))
cat(tab(blank_repeats(pos_tab, "Model"), digits = 1, caption = tn("Simulated windows by position: coverage of the true daily new infections, and the error of the starting state (percentage points)")), sep = "\n")
```

## Real data

```{r renewal-real, results="asis"}
ra <- real_ok[real_ok$method %in% c("BiLSTM", "ABC-MCMC"), ]
row_r <- function(d, label, M, g) data.frame(Model = M, Data = g, Approach = label, `Coverage (%)` = mean(d$coverage),
  `Interval score` = mean(d$interval_score), `Coverage: next 14 days` = mean(d$cov_future, na.rm = TRUE),
  `Interval score: next 14 days` = mean(d[[if ("is_future" %in% names(d)) "is_future" else "IS_future"]], na.rm = TRUE), check.names = FALSE)
groups <- list(`US states` = function(d) d$group == "US states", `Utah and Baltimore` = function(d) d$group == "Utah and Baltimore",
               `Utah COVID-19 only` = function(d) grepl("Utah COVID", d$wave))
rr_tab <- do.call(rbind, lapply(names(INFO), function(M) do.call(rbind, lapply(names(groups), function(g) {
  sel <- groups[[g]]
  a <- ra[ra$model == M & sel(ra), ]
  r <- ren_real[ren_real$model == M & sel(ren_real), ]
  r$coverage <- r$cov_new; r$interval_score <- r$IS_new
  rbind(row_r(a[a$method == "BiLSTM", ], "BiLSTM, model 500 runs", M, g),
        do.call(rbind, lapply(unique(r$approach), function(x) row_r(r[r$approach == x, ], paste("BiLSTM,", x), M, g))),
        row_r(a[a$method == "ABC-MCMC", ], "ABC-MCMC, model 500 runs", M, g))
}))))
rr_tab$Data[duplicated(paste(rr_tab$Model, rr_tab$Data))] <- ""
rr_tab <- blank_repeats(rr_tab, "Model")
cat(tab(rr_tab, digits = 1, caption = tn("Real data: coverage and interval score of the observed daily counts in the window and in the 14 days after it")), sep = "\n")
```

```{r renewal-examples, fig.width=14, fig.height=7, fig.cap=fc("SEIR on Utah COVID-19, 60-day windows. Blue: observed; green: BiLSTM, model 500 runs; dark blue dashed: renewal A; orange dotted: renewal B. Titles: coverage of model runs | renewal A | renewal B.")}
rbil <- readRDS(file.path(REAL, "bilstm_fits.rds"))
op <- par(mfrow = c(2, 3), mar = c(2.5, 4, 3, 0.5))
set.seed(5)
for (wv in c("Utah COVID-19 2024-25", "Utah COVID-19 summer 2023")) for (pos in POSITIONS) {
  w <- Filter(function(z) z$wave == wv && z$length == 60 && z$position == pos, rwin)[[1]]
  info <- model_info("SEIR"); f <- rbil[[paste("SEIR", w$id)]]; i <- seq_len(w$length)
  bA <- renewal_band(info, f$draws, w$length)$new
  R0s <- stats::quantile(vapply(f$draws, function(p) p$ptran * p$crate / p$recov, 0), seq(0.02, 0.98, length.out = n_b), names = FALSE)
  bB <- renewal_band(info, lapply(R0s, function(r) renewal_initial_state(info, w$y, r, w$known[info$known])), w$length)$new
  bM <- rfit("SEIR", w$id, "BiLSTM")$band[i, ]
  cv <- c(mean(w$y >= bM$lower & w$y <= bM$upper), mean(w$y >= bA$lower & w$y <= bA$upper), mean(w$y >= bB$lower & w$y <= bB$upper))
  top <- max(c(w$y, bM$upper, bA$upper, bB$upper))
  plot(w$x, w$y, type = "n", ylim = c(0, top), xlab = "", ylab = "daily count", cex.main = 0.85,
       main = sprintf("%s, %s\n%.0f%% | %.0f%% | %.0f%%", wv, pos, 100 * cv[1], 100 * cv[2], 100 * cv[3]))
  polygon(c(w$x, rev(w$x)), c(bM$upper, rev(bM$lower)), col = adjustcolor("forestgreen", 0.25), border = NA)
  lines(w$x, bA$upper, col = "navy", lty = 2); lines(w$x, bA$lower, col = "navy", lty = 2); lines(w$x, bA$median, col = "navy", lwd = 1.5)
  lines(w$x, bB$upper, col = "darkorange", lty = 3, lwd = 1.5); lines(w$x, bB$lower, col = "darkorange", lty = 3, lwd = 1.5)
  lines(w$x, bB$median, col = "darkorange", lwd = 1.5)
  lines(w$x, w$y, col = "blue", lwd = 1.3)
}
par(op)
```

# Computational cost

The BiLSTM has a **one-time cost** (simulating its training epidemics and training the
networks) and then costs almost nothing per window. The other methods cost the same for every
window, because each window needs its own thousands of model runs.

## Time per window

Each baseline ran on one CPU core per window. The BiLSTM's time is one network pass over all
windows of a model on the CPU, divided by the number of windows (a single window on its own
takes about 0.05-0.1 seconds, mostly loading).

```{r cost-window, results="asis"}
per <- function(d, M, m, col) mean(d[[col]][d$model == M & d$method == m], na.rm = TRUE)
cw <- data.frame(Method = METHODS,
  `Simulated, SEIR: seconds` = sapply(METHODS, function(m) per(sbr_ok, "SEIR", m, "seconds")),
  `Simulated, SIR: seconds` = sapply(METHODS, function(m) per(sbr_ok, "SIR", m, "seconds")),
  `Real data, SEIR: seconds` = sapply(METHODS, function(m) per(real_ok, "SEIR", m, "seconds")),
  `Real data, SIR: seconds` = sapply(METHODS, function(m) per(real_ok, "SIR", m, "seconds")),
  `Simulated, SEIR: model runs` = sapply(METHODS, function(m) per(sbr_ok, "SEIR", m, "model_runs")),
  `Simulated, SIR: model runs` = sapply(METHODS, function(m) per(sbr_ok, "SIR", m, "model_runs")),
  check.names = FALSE)
cat(tab(cw, digits = 3, caption = tn("Mean seconds and model runs per window")), sep = "\n")
```

## The BiLSTM's one-time cost

```{r cost-once, results="asis"}
tc <- read.csv(file.path(OUT, "bilstm_training_cost.csv"))
once <- do.call(rbind, lapply(names(INFO), function(M) {
  d <- tc[tc$model == M, ]
  data.frame(Model = M, `Training epidemics` = format(d$bank_simulations[1], big.mark = ","),
             `Simulating them: hours on 32 cores` = d$bank_wall_hours[1],
             `Simulating them: CPU-hours` = d$bank_wall_hours[1] * d$bank_cores[1],
             `Training: hours per network` = sprintf("%.1f-%.1f", min(d$training_hours), max(d$training_hours)),
             `Training: GPU-hours for 5 networks` = sum(d$training_hours),
             `GPUs used` = paste(unique(d$gpu), collapse = ", "), check.names = FALSE)
}))
cat(tab(once, digits = 1, caption = tn("One-time cost of the BiLSTM (from the training logs)")), sep = "\n")
```

Training time depends mostly on the GPU: a network took about 4-5 hours on a recent GPU (RTX
3090, V100) and up to 20 hours on the older GPUs (GTX Titan X) that were free at the time; a
model with fewer networks, or one network, costs proportionally less.

## Total for this report

```{r cost-total, results="asis"}
tot <- data.frame(Method = METHODS,
  `Windows` = sapply(METHODS, function(m) sum(sbr_ok$method == m) + sum(real_ok$method == m)),
  `CPU-hours for all windows` = sapply(METHODS, function(m) (sum(sbr_ok$seconds[sbr_ok$method == m]) +
                                                              sum(real_ok$seconds[real_ok$method == m])) / 3600),
  check.names = FALSE)
cat(tab(tot, digits = 2, caption = tn("Compute used for all simulated and real windows of this report (SEIR and SIR)")), sep = "\n")
sim_cpu <- sum(tapply(tc$bank_wall_hours * tc$bank_cores, tc$model, `[`, 1))
per_win <- function(m) mean(c(sbr_ok$seconds[sbr_ok$method == m], real_ok$seconds[real_ok$method == m])) / 3600
```

Simulating the training data of both models took `r round(sim_cpu)` CPU-hours, the same as
about `r format(round(sim_cpu / per_win("DE")), big.mark = ",")` windows with DE,
`r format(round(sim_cpu / per_win("ABC-SMC")), big.mark = ",")` with ABC-SMC or
`r format(round(sim_cpu / per_win("ABC-MCMC")), big.mark = ",")` with ABC-MCMC, plus the GPU
training. After that, every new window costs a fraction of a second, so the BiLSTM pays off
when many windows or datasets are calibrated (or when an answer is needed at once), and the
same trained model can be shared and used by others without any of this cost.

# Conclusions

- On **noise-free simulated data**, both models estimate **R0** accurately from any part of an
  epidemic, and longer windows give better estimates. Short windows are harder for SEIR than
  for SIR, probably because the incubation period hides part of the early growth.
- **ptran and crate** are not identifiable from case curves: only R0 = ptran x crate / recov
  is. To estimate them separately, one of them (for example the contact rate from a contact
  survey) must be given.
- The models **recover the whole epidemic** in simulation, including the number currently
  infected.
- **Against standard calibration methods** with default settings (ABC-MCMC, ABC-SMC, DE,
  Nelder-Mead), on simulated windows where the truth is known, the BiLSTM recovers R0, the
  starting state and the hidden number currently infected best, and is thousands of times
  faster. The baselines come close only near the beginning of an epidemic; DE matches the
  observed curve about as closely. ABC-SMC finishes only with more model runs than its default
  limit allows.
- **Ease of use:** the BiLSTM needs only the daily counts and the known values. Every baseline
  needs ranges for R0 and for the starting state, its own settings, and seconds to minutes of
  model runs for every window.
- **Improving the BiLSTM:** more training epidemics and a falling learning rate helped a
  little; tuning alone did not. Windows from the end of an epidemic did not improve with any
  change.
- On **real data**, the noise-free BiLSTM covers COVID-19 waves of daily-reporting US states
  about as well as ABC-MCMC and ABC-SMC, and better than DE and Nelder-Mead; on the Utah and
  Baltimore data, and most of all on Utah COVID-19 cases, ABC-MCMC, which fits each curve
  directly, is clearly best: weekday patterns, reporting spikes and repeated waves are not in
  noise-free training data.
- **Next steps for real data:** cleaner real data that suit a noise-free model (daily hospital
  admissions), and training with a reporting model (a reported share, a weekly pattern and
  extra noise), which earlier models (SEIR v5 and v6) used with 93-98% coverage on influenza
  seasons and COVID-19 waves of single states.

# Using the package: a guide

Everything in this report can be done with the R package **epiworldRcalibrate**. This section
shows how, step by step. The code below runs as part of this report (the slow steps are saved
after the first run). A longer tutorial, with installation details and troubleshooting, is
`TUTORIAL.Rmd` in the package folder; the help pages (`?window_calibrator`, ...) describe every
function and setting.

```{r guide-setup, include=FALSE}
GUIDE_CACHE <- file.path(normalizePath(OUT), "guide_cache", "")
CORES <- as.integer(Sys.getenv("SLURM_CPUS_PER_TASK", "4"))
# methods_common.R (sourced for the renewal section) has its own score_band(); the guide uses the package's.
if (exists("score_band", envir = globalenv(), inherits = FALSE)) rm(score_band, envir = globalenv())
```

## Installing

```{r guide-install, echo=TRUE, eval=FALSE}
install.packages(c("remotes", "DEoptim"))
remotes::install_github("UofUEpiBio/epiworldRcalibrate")   # or remotes::install_local("path/to/epiworldRcalibrate")
library(epiworldRcalibrate)
```

The BiLSTM runs in Python (PyTorch) through `reticulate`, which sets up the Python packages
it needs the first time (or set `RETICULATE_PYTHON` to a Python with `torch` before loading
the package). The trained SEIR and SIR models come with the package.

## Data shipped with the package

| Dataset | What it is |
|---|---|
| `covid_us_states` | daily COVID-19 cases in the 50 states and DC, 2020-2023 (Johns Hopkins University), with populations |
| `covid_utah` | daily COVID-19 cases in Utah, 2020-2025 (Utah DHHS) |
| `admissions_utah` | daily influenza and COVID-19 hospital admissions in Utah, 2020-2024 (HHS) |
| `flu_baltimore_1918` | daily influenza cases in Baltimore, 1918 |
| `real_data_waves` | the 35 waves of this report, with the population size and known values used for each |

`wave_data()` gives the daily counts of one wave and `real_data_windows()` cuts windows from
the beginning, middle and end of the waves; with its defaults it gives the 315 real-data
windows of this report.

```{r guide-data, echo=TRUE}
real_data_waves[c(1:3, 31:35), c("wave", "dataset", "start", "end", "n", "recov", "incub")]
w <- real_data_windows("New York Omicron 2021-22", lengths = 60, positions = "middle")[[1]]
str(w[c("cases", "future", "n", "recov", "incub", "wave", "position")])
```

## Calibrating a window with the BiLSTM

`calibrate(daily counts, method, known values)`. The result has R0 with its 95% range, ptran
and crate, and the state on the first day of the window:

```{r guide-bilstm, echo=TRUE}
bilstm <- window_calibrator("SEIR")        # window_calibrator("SIR") for the SIR model (no incub)
fit <- calibrate(w$cases, bilstm, n = w$n, recov = w$recov, incub = w$incub)
fit
calibration_estimate(fit)                  # the estimates as a named vector
```

## Calibrating with ABC-MCMC, ABC-SMC, DE or Nelder-Mead

`window_baselines()` gives the four standard methods with the settings of this report (Section
"The methods compared"). They are used with `calibrate()` like the BiLSTM; each takes seconds
to minutes, so here they run in parallel:

```{r guide-baselines, echo=TRUE, cache=TRUE, cache.path=GUIDE_CACHE}
baselines <- window_baselines("SEIR")      # a list: ABC-MCMC, ABC-SMC, DE, NelderMead
fits <- parallel::mclapply(baselines, function(b) calibrate(w$cases, b, n = w$n, recov = w$recov, incub = w$incub),
                           mc.cores = min(4, CORES))
fits <- c(list(BiLSTM = fit), fits)
```

```{r guide-fits-table, echo=TRUE}
t(sapply(fits, function(f) c(f$estimate[c("R0", "ptran", "crate")], R0_low = f$intervals["R0", 1],
                             R0_high = f$intervals["R0", 2], seconds = f$diagnostics$seconds,
                             model_runs = f$diagnostics$model_runs)))
```

The BiLSTM's time includes loading Python and the networks, which happens once per session;
after that it takes a fraction of a second per window (Section "Computational cost"). The
standard methods search R0 with the contact rate fixed at the middle of its range (10 for
SEIR), so their crate is always 10. Settings are changed by method name, for example
`window_baselines("SEIR", settings = list(DE = list(itermax = 400)))`; `?window_baselines`
lists them all.

## Predicting and scoring

`predict_cases()` turns any fit into a 95% band of the daily new infections, in the window and
`ahead` days after it, by 500 runs of the epiworldR model from the estimated state
(`method = "renewal"` uses the renewal equation instead, about 200 times faster).
`plot_bands()` shows the bands of several methods with their coverage and interval score:

```{r guide-bands, echo=TRUE, cache=TRUE, cache.path=GUIDE_CACHE}
bands <- lapply(fits, predict_cases, ahead = 14)
```

```{r guide-bands-plot, echo=TRUE, fig.width=12, fig.height=7, fig.cap=fc("plot_bands(): the 95% bands of each method on a 60-day window around the peak of the Omicron wave in New York (cases per 10,000 people), with the 14 days after it (open points).")}
scores <- plot_bands(bands, future = w$future)
```

```{r guide-scores, echo=TRUE}
scores                                      # the coverage and interval score shown in the panels
score_band(bands$BiLSTM)                    # one band: coverage, width, error of the median, interval score
interval_score(y = 35, lower = 10, upper = 30)   # one day: the width 20 plus 40 x the miss of 5
```

```{r guide-window-context}
mid60 <- real_ok[real_ok$model == "SEIR" & real_ok$group == "US states" & real_ok$length == 60 &
                 real_ok$position == "middle", ]
mid_cov <- tapply(mid60$coverage, mid60$method, mean)
```

This window, around the peak of the wave, is a hard one: the BiLSTM expects the epidemic to keep
growing, and every method misses the sharp fall after the peak. It was picked to show the code,
not as a typical case: over all `r nrow(mid60) / length(unique(mid60$method))` 60-day windows from
the middle of US-state waves, the BiLSTM covered `r pct(mid_cov[["BiLSTM"]])` of the days,
ABC-MCMC `r pct(mid_cov[["ABC-MCMC"]])`, ABC-SMC `r pct(mid_cov[["ABC-SMC"]])`, DE
`r pct(mid_cov[["DE"]])` and Nelder-Mead `r pct(mid_cov[["NelderMead"]])` (Section "Real data").
The code here gives the same results as that comparison for this window (for example the
BiLSTM's R0 of `r f2(fit$estimate[["R0"]])`).

## Estimating ptran and crate

With `unknowns = "ptran_crate"`, the standard methods search ptran and crate instead of R0, and
the ABC methods give a 95% range for each. On a simulated window with known values, the
accepted values lie along the curve of constant R0 = ptran x crate / recov: the data fix R0, not
ptran and crate.

```{r guide-ptran-crate, echo=TRUE, cache=TRUE, cache.path=GUIDE_CACHE}
# A simulated SEIR epidemic with known values, and 60 days from its middle.
true <- list(n = 8000, recov = 1 / 7, incub = 5, R0 = 2.5, crate = 10)
true$ptran <- true$R0 * true$recov / true$crate
m <- epiworldR::ModelSEIRCONN("example", n = true$n, prevalence = 0.002, contact_rate = true$crate,
                              incubation_days = true$incub, transmission_rate = true$ptran, recovery_rate = true$recov)
epiworldR::verbose_off(m)
epiworldR::run(m, ndays = 150, seed = 42)
tr <- epiworldR::get_hist_transition_matrix(m)
tr <- tr[tr$state_from == "Exposed" & tr$state_to == "Infected", ]
sim_window <- tr$counts[match(41:100, tr$date)]
sim_window[is.na(sim_window)] <- 0

free <- window_baselines("SEIR", methods = c("ABC-MCMC", "ABC-SMC"), unknowns = "ptran_crate")
fits_free <- parallel::mclapply(free, function(b) calibrate(sim_window, b, n = 8000, recov = 1 / 7, incub = 5),
                                mc.cores = min(2, CORES))
fits_free$BiLSTM <- calibrate(sim_window, bilstm, n = 8000, recov = 1 / 7, incub = 5)
```

```{r guide-ptran-crate-plot, echo=TRUE, fig.width=13, fig.height=4.2, fig.cap=fc("plot_ptran_crate(): accepted values of ptran and crate (points) lie along the curve of constant R0 (dashed: the estimated R0; orange: the true values and their R0). The BiLSTM picks a typical ptran and the matching crate.")}
lapply(fits_free, function(f) signif(f$intervals, 3))   # 95% ranges of R0, ptran and crate
plot_ptran_crate(fits_free[c("BiLSTM", "ABC-MCMC", "ABC-SMC")], truth = c(ptran = true$ptran, crate = true$crate))
```

## Comparing methods on many windows

`compare_methods()` runs every method on every window and scores each one; it is how the
comparisons of this report can be repeated. A window is a list with `cases`, the known values,
and optionally `future` (the counts after it), the truth (`R0`, `ptran`, `crate`, `state`) and
labels such as `position`. `plot_comparison()` and `plot_estimates()` show the results.

```{r guide-compare, echo=TRUE, eval=FALSE}
windows <- real_data_windows()                           # the 315 real-data windows of this report
results <- compare_methods(windows, "SEIR", cores = 32)  # BiLSTM + the four standard methods
plot_comparison(results)                                 # errors, coverage, interval score, time
plot_estimates(results, "R0")                            # R0 and 95% ranges, window by window
```

```{r guide-as-compare}
# The comparisons of this report (Sections 4 and 5), in the format of compare_methods().
sim_results <- data.frame(model = sbr$model, window = sbr$id, position = sbr$position, method = sbr$method,
                          failed = sbr$failed, days = sbr$length, R0 = sbr$R0, R0_low = sbr$R0_low,
                          R0_high = sbr$R0_high, R0_true = sbr$R0_true, R0_error = abs(sbr$R0 - sbr$R0_true),
                          state_error = sbr$state_error, coverage = sbr$cov_new, interval_score = sbr$IS_new,
                          coverage_ahead = sbr$cov_future, interval_score_ahead = sbr$IS_future,
                          seconds = sbr$seconds, model_runs = sbr$model_runs)
real_results <- data.frame(model = real$model, window = real$id, group = real$group, wave = real$wave,
                           position = real$position, method = real$method, failed = real$failed, days = real$length,
                           R0 = real$R0, R0_low = real$R0_low, R0_high = real$R0_high, coverage = real$coverage,
                           interval_score = real$interval_score, coverage_ahead = real$cov_future,
                           interval_score_ahead = real$is_future, seconds = real$seconds, model_runs = real$model_runs)
sim_results$method <- factor(sim_results$method, METHODS); sim_results <- sim_results[order(sim_results$method), ]
real_results$method <- factor(real_results$method, METHODS); real_results <- real_results[order(real_results$method), ]
sim_results$method <- as.character(sim_results$method); real_results$method <- as.character(real_results$method)
```

The figures below are made by these plot functions from the comparisons of this report (same
methods and settings), turned into the format of `compare_methods()` (`sim_results`: the 216
simulated windows; `real_results`: the 630 real-data windows). Small points: windows; large
points: the mean (blue: the BiLSTM); orange line: 95% coverage.

```{r guide-plot-sim-seir, echo=TRUE, fig.width=13, fig.height=7, fig.cap=fc("plot_comparison() on the 108 simulated SEIR windows: R0 error, starting-state error, coverage and interval score of the true daily new infections in the window, coverage of the 14 days after it, and seconds per window.")}
plot_comparison(sim_results[sim_results$model == "SEIR", ])
```

```{r guide-plot-sim-sir, echo=TRUE, fig.width=13, fig.height=7, fig.cap=fc("The same for the 108 simulated SIR windows.")}
plot_comparison(sim_results[sim_results$model == "SIR", ])
```

```{r guide-plot-estimates, echo=TRUE, fig.width=13, fig.height=3.8, fig.cap=fc("plot_estimates(): R0 and its 95% range by method for three simulated SEIR windows of 61 days (beginning, middle and end of an epidemic); orange: the true R0. DE and Nelder-Mead give no range.")}
d <- sim_results[sim_results$model == "SEIR" & sim_results$days == 61, ]
plot_estimates(d, "R0", windows = tapply(d$window, d$position, `[`, 1)[c("beginning", "middle", "end")])
```

```{r guide-plot-real-us, echo=TRUE, fig.width=13, fig.height=3.8, fig.cap=fc("plot_comparison() on the 270 real-data SEIR windows from US states: coverage and interval score of the observed counts in the window, coverage of the 14 days after it, and seconds per window.")}
measures <- c("coverage", "interval_score", "coverage_ahead", "seconds")
plot_comparison(real_results[real_results$model == "SEIR" & real_results$group == "US states", ], measures, ncol = 4)
```

```{r guide-plot-real-utah, echo=TRUE, fig.width=13, fig.height=3.8, fig.cap=fc("The same for the 45 SEIR windows from Utah and Baltimore.")}
plot_comparison(real_results[real_results$model == "SEIR" & real_results$group == "Utah and Baltimore", ], measures,
                ncol = 4)
```

For the SIR model, use `model == "SIR"`.

## Making your own BiLSTM

For other ranges of the parameters, simulate training epidemics, tune the network settings
(optional) and train; then use the new model like the shipped one:

```{r guide-train, echo=TRUE, eval=FALSE}
data <- simulate_window_data("SEIR", n_sims = 1e6, output_dir = "my_seir_data", priors = list(R0 = c(0.8, 3)),
                             cores = 32)
best <- tune_window_calibrator(data, output_dir = "my_seir_tuning", n_trials = 40)
train_window_calibrator(data, output_dir = "my_seir_model", hyperparameters = best, seeds = 1:5)
my_bilstm <- window_calibrator("SEIR", model_dir = "my_seir_model")
```

The shipped models took about 2 hours on 32 cores to simulate (SEIR) and about 4 hours per
network on a recent GPU to train (Section "Computational cost").

## All functions and data

| Function | What it does |
|---|---|
| `window_calibrator(model)` | the trained BiLSTM for SEIR or SIR windows (or your own with `model_dir`) |
| `window_baselines(model, methods, settings, unknowns)` | ABC-MCMC, ABC-SMC, DE and Nelder-Mead, set up as in this report; `unknowns = "ptran_crate"` searches ptran and crate |
| `calibrate(cases, method, n, recov, incub)` | fit a window with any of them |
| `calibration_estimate(fit)` | the estimates as a named vector |
| `predict_cases(fit, ahead, method)` | 95% bands by model runs or the renewal equation |
| `coverage()`, `interval_score()`, `score_band()` | how well a band matches the data |
| `compare_methods(windows, model, calibrators, cores)` | all methods on many windows, with errors, coverage, interval scores and time |
| `plot_bands()`, `plot_comparison()`, `plot_estimates()`, `plot_ptran_crate()` | plots to compare methods |
| `wave_data()`, `real_data_windows()` | the counts of a real wave; windows of real data |
| `covid_us_states`, `covid_utah`, `admissions_utah`, `flu_baltimore_1918`, `real_data_waves` | real data |
| `simulate_window_data()`, `tune_window_calibrator()`, `train_window_calibrator()` | make your own BiLSTM |
